title: Hybridisation sp sp2 sp3 Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Two paints mix into one new colour, four scoops blend into one milkshake, and methane has four perfectly equal bonds. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 4, Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure) we learn hybridisation: an atom mixes its orbitals into equal new hybrid orbitals.

On the molecule bench, carbon promotes a 2s electron, mixes one s and three p orbitals into four sp3 orbitals and points them to a tetrahedron at 109.5°. Then sp2 (120°, BCl3) and sp (180°, BeCl2) with their s character, the rules of mixing link by link, sp3d in PCl5 step by step, sp3d2 in SF6, and lone pairs in NH3 and H2O. Then the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 48 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:

1:40 sp2 and sp: fewer orbitals mixed
2:01 Pause and think: s character
2:20 The rules of mixing, link by link
2:57 Worked example: sp3d in PCl5
3:34 sp3d2 and lone pairs
4:07 Exam trap: carbon in ethyne
4:33 Practice question (NEET pattern)
